newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Arrest order against Colombian army chief lifted.
newsitem.headline: Arrest order against Colombian army chief lifted.

text.p: An arrest order hanging over the commander of the Colombian army because of his efforts to quell a peasant uprising was lifted by a provincial court on Monday, judicial sources said.

A higher court overturned the arrest warrant served by a local judge in southern Caqueta province, after General Harold Bedoya failed to order the removal of barricades blocking the advance of thousands of peasant farmers protesting the compulsory eradication of coca plantations in the region.
In an interview with Colombia's RCN radio on Sunday, Bedoya said of the 30-day arrest warrant: "If we carry on like that, the army will virtually be forbidden to operate.
"If there are no laws and policies to wage war then we cannot confront the guerrilla threat," he added.

When the order was issued 10 days ago against Bedoya and regional commander General Nestor Ramirez, Colombian landowners and some political commentators said leftist rebels, linked to cocaine trafficking, had leaned on the judge to order the generals' arrests.

The government ordered an inquiry into what had prompted the judge's original decision. Civilian courts were given wider powers of jurisdiction over the military in a package of reforms in 1991, aimed at improving respect for human rights.
Judicial sources said on Monday: "The court in Belen de los Andaquies has totally revoked the ruling issued by the lower court in Albania."
The legal controversy came amid one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in decades, which left some military experts questioning whether the army was still in control of the situation.
The authorities had accused the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) of inciting the peasant mobilisations in Caqueta, and other coca-growing provinces.
